newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Four Strathcona test drills at Busang completed.
newsitem.headline: Four Strathcona test drills at Busang completed.

text.p: Canadian mining consultant Strathcona Mineral Services has completed four of its six test drillings at the Busang gold site in East Kalimantan, a spokeswoman for the Busang partners said on Friday.
"Four drillings have been completed and the results are being stored at a (locked) hangar in Balikpapan (in East Kalimantan)," Nia Sarinastiti told Reuters.

She was speaking on behalf of the Busang Indonesian Gold JV consortium formed on February 17 to develop the Busang property. Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd has a 45-percent stake in Busang, Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc of the U.S. 15 percent and Indonesian interests the rest.
Sarinastiti said Strathcona, a Toronto-based company hired by Bre-X to carry out an independent audit of Busang, was in the process of drilling the fifth hole.
Strathcona planned to drill six holes to determine the amount of gold contained in the Busang deposit.
Bre-X shocked the mining community with a statement last month which said there was a possibility that the amount of gold at Busang had been overstated.
It had earlier put gold reserves at some 71 million ounces, which would have made it the biggest find of the century.
Sarinastiti said the test drillings were expected to be completed as scheduled by the middle of this month, and the samples flown to a laboratory in Perth, Australia.
"The samples will be crushed at the laboratory in Perth and parcels of the samples will be sent to local company Indo Assay's laboratory in Balikpapan for testing," she said.
She said the samples could also be be sent to a laboratory in Singapore. "There's a possibility samples would be sent to a laboratory in Singapore and the one in Perth."
Sarinastiti said the laboratory testing was expected to be completed by end-April and the results were likely to be known by the first week of May.

Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said in Toronto on Thursday the company had the money to weather the storm over the Busang discovery and vowed the audit would prove he made the century's richest gold strike.
Bre-X has been in the eye of a storm since preliminary tests by its partner Freeport at Busang indicated the property might contain "insignificant" amounts of gold.
The announcement prompted panic selling of Bre-X shares last month, lopping almost C$3 billion ($2.2 billion), or more than 80 percent, from the company's stock market value.
